We killed our AI strategy last week.

Nobody noticed.

Not the board, not the two customers who asked for it in Q2, not the intern who wrote the deck. The Notion page still says "AI-first" in the header and 14 people have it bookmarked.

What we actually did: we deleted the roadmap column called "AI initiatives" and moved the three things in it into the columns where they belonged. Search got the embedding upgrade because search was slow. Support got the draft-reply button because Priya was answering 60 tickets a day by hand. The "AI agent for onboarding" went nowhere, because nobody could say what it was for.

The strategy was a folder. The work was already happening in other folders.

I think most companies our size have the same folder. It exists so that someone can point at it when a customer or an investor asks. Delete it and check whether anything stops. In our case, the only thing that stopped was a weekly meeting.

We kept the meeting slot for lunch.
